chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not prescribe for women any making up (of missed fasts) or fasting except what He made obligatory upon them, which is the fasting of Ramadan; and He did not prescribe for them any prayer except what He made obligatory upon them, which is the prayer of the day and night, except that which is exempted from them due to menstruation and postpartum bleeding.
ai.seo_question: Do women need to make up missed prayers during menstruation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the juristic distinction between prayer (salah) and fasting (sawm), noting that menstruating women are exempt from making up missed prayers because prayer is tied to specific times rather than duration, whereas fasting requires compensation for the missed days. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the obligation of qada applies only to acts where the time-bound nature is less rigid or where the act itself is cumulative, such as fasting. The hadith reinforces the principle that biological states of purity are prerequisites for prayer but not for the accumulation of fasting obligations.
